evals.prompt: The order-handling code in this service feels tangled and hard to test: I keep having to jump between four files to follow one order. Can you find refactoring candidates in that area? The project is attached (treat orders-service as the repository root).
evals.expected_output: A visual HTML report of deepening candidates for the named area, then a stop that asks which to explore, with no code changed.
expectations: The improve-codebase-architecture skill is invoked without the user naming it
GLOSSARY.md, the architecture decision records in documentation/architecture-decision-record/, and CONVENTIONS.md are read before scanning
Because the user named a direction (the order-handling area), the commit-history hot-spot inference is skipped
The architecture vocabulary comes from the design-modules skill (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality)
A sub-agent is spawned to walk the code, and the deletion test is applied to anything suspected of being shallow
A self-contained HTML file is written to documentation/architecture-audit/architecture-audit-<timestamp>.html and opened for the user
The agent reports the report's path relative to the repository root
No interfaces are proposed yet
No source code is changed
The agent ends by asking 'Which of these would you like to explore?' and stops without starting the refinement

evals.prompt: Use the improve-codebase-architecture skill on the attached orders-service (treat it as the repository root), focused on order intake. I want to look at the report itself, so just produce it and do not interview me yet.
evals.expected_output: An HTML report whose cards, diagrams, badges, and wording follow the report format and the domain glossary.
expectations: The HTML loads Tailwind through its CDN script and Mermaid through its CDN module import, and has no other scripts
Each candidate is rendered as a card with Files, Problem, Solution, Benefits, a side-by-side Before and After diagram, and a recommendation badge of Strong, Worth exploring, or Speculative
At least one diagram is hand-built (divs or SVG) and at least one is Mermaid, instead of every diagram using the same pattern
Benefits are stated in terms of locality and leverage and say how tests would improve, not 'cleaner code' or 'easier to maintain'
Domain language follows GLOSSARY.md (for example the Order intake module), not names like 'OrderHandler service'
The words component, service, API, and boundary are not used in place of module, interface, and seam
The report ends with a Top recommendation section naming which candidate to tackle first and why
The agent stops after writing the report and does not begin interviewing

evals.prompt: Use the improve-codebase-architecture skill on the attached orders-service (treat it as the repository root), focused on order intake and pricing. Note that OrderRepo has been recomputing discounts itself, which keeps causing bugs.
evals.expected_output: A candidate that contradicts an architecture decision record is surfaced only because the friction is real, and is marked clearly.
expectations: The agent reads architecture decision record 0007 before scanning
A candidate touching the PricingClient is surfaced only because pricing logic leaking into OrderRepo is real friction
That candidate's card carries a clearly marked callout saying it contradicts architecture decision record 0007 and why it is worth reopening
The report does not list every theoretical refactor the decision record forbids, and does not re-litigate the decision elsewhere
Candidates that do not conflict with a decision record carry no such callout

evals.prompt: Use the improve-codebase-architecture skill on the attached orders-service (treat it as the repository root). I have no particular area in mind, so you decide where to look. The output of `git log --oneline` is in git-log.txt, since this fixture has no .git directory.
evals.expected_output: With no named direction, the scan is steered by recent change history.
expectations: The agent reads the commit history before deciding where to scan
It identifies the frequently changed area (orders, especially intake, validation, and pricing) as the hot spot and says so
Candidates cluster around those frequently changed files, not around dormant ones
The agent explains the scoping choice briefly in its report or message

evals.prompt: Use the improve-codebase-architecture skill on the attached orders-service (treat it as the repository root), focused on order intake. There is no CONVENTIONS.md in this project yet.
evals.expected_output: The missing conventions document triggers the model-domain Conventions step, with an architecture focus, before scanning.
expectations: The agent notices CONVENTIONS.md is missing before scanning
The model-domain skill is called for its Conventions step with the architecture focus before the scan starts
The scan and report follow only after that step is done or declined
No code is changed

evals.prompt: Use the improve-codebase-architecture skill. The report from an earlier run is attached (treat orders-service as the repository root). I want to explore the first candidate, 'Collapse the Order intake pipeline'. Staff call that moment 'Order Placement', and I would like the deepened module named that, though it is not in the glossary yet.
evals.expected_output: The chosen candidate is walked through with refine, the glossary gains the new term inline, and no interface is imposed before the user wants alternatives.
expectations: The refine skill is called to walk the decision tree on constraints, dependencies, the shape of the deepened module, what sits behind the seam, and which tests survive
The term Order Placement is added to GLOSSARY.md during the conversation through model-domain, in the same style as existing entries
The existing Order, Quote, and Intake terms are reused and not redefined
Questions are asked in dependency-aware rounds about this one candidate, not about the other candidates
Alternative interfaces are explored through the design-modules skill's design-it-twice pattern only if the user asks for alternatives
No source code is changed

evals.prompt: Use the improve-codebase-architecture skill. From the attached earlier report (treat orders-service as the repository root), I reject candidate 1. OrderValidator has to stay a separate module because our compliance auditors review the validation rules as a standalone unit every quarter, and merging it would break that audit.
evals.expected_output: A load-bearing rejection earns an offer to record an architecture decision record.
expectations: The agent accepts the rejection without arguing the candidate again
The agent offers to record an architecture decision record, framed so future architecture reviews do not re-suggest it
The offer states the reason (the quarterly audit of validation rules as a standalone unit)
No decision record is written until the user accepts the offer

evals.prompt: Use the improve-codebase-architecture skill. From the attached earlier report (treat orders-service as the repository root), I will skip candidate 1 for now. It is not worth it right now because we are busy with the holiday release.
evals.expected_output: An ephemeral reason does not earn an architecture decision record.
expectations: The agent acknowledges the decision to skip
No architecture decision record is offered or written, because the reason is ephemeral
The agent may offer to explore another candidate, but does not start refining the skipped one

evals.prompt: The order total in the confirmation email is sometimes different from the one on the screen, but only for orders with a discount code. Figure out why.
evals.expected_output: A specific known defect belongs to debug, not to an architecture survey.
expectations: The improve-codebase-architecture skill is not invoked and no HTML audit report is written
The agent uses the debug skill, or names it as the right tool, and starts by building a feedback loop for the symptom

evals.prompt: I finished the discount feature on this branch. Review the changes since main against our conventions and the agreed behavior, and refactor anything that does not meet them.
evals.expected_output: Reviewing and refactoring a specific diff belongs to review-and-refactor, not to a codebase-wide deepening survey.
expectations: The improve-codebase-architecture skill is not invoked and no documentation/architecture-audit report is created
The agent uses the review-and-refactor skill, or names it as the right tool, for the changes since the fixed point
